title: prometheus_metrics plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `prometheus_metrics` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component PrometheusMetricsConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

PrometheusMetricsConfig.description: Plugin: prometheus_metrics — Exports gateway metrics in Prometheus format. Null or an empty object uses defaults. At most one enabled instance is permitted and it must use global scope because the registry and tunables are process-wide. Unknown keys are rejected. `schema` and `schema_ref` are not accepted properties.

render_cache_ttl_seconds.description: How long the cached /metrics response is served before rebuilding (seconds)

stale_entry_ttl_seconds.description: How long idle metric entries live before eviction (seconds). Prevents unbounded memory growth from deleted/recreated proxies

mesh_series_budget_per_family.description: Hard ceiling on live MeshRequestKey series retained per mesh metric family in the process-wide MetricsRegistry. Shared by ordinary mesh identity dimensions and CEL-derived dimensions: newly observed keys beyond the budget are dropped until stale_entry_ttl_seconds eviction frees capacity, and counted on ferrum_mesh_metric_series_overflow_total{family}. 0 is rejected — there is no unlimited mode.

cache_invalidation_min_age_ms.description: Minimum age (ms) of the render cache before record() will invalidate it. Under extreme load this prevents an allocation per request

request_duration_buckets_ms.description: Finite bucket upper bounds (milliseconds) for the request-scoped duration histograms ferrum_request_duration_ms, ferrum_backend_duration_ms, ferrum_edge_overhead_ms, and ferrum_mesh_request_duration_ms. Must be strictly increasing (enforced by the plugin constructor); the +Inf bucket is implicit. Changing the layout drops the affected histogram series, which restart under the new layout.

session_duration_buckets_ms.description: Finite bucket upper bounds (milliseconds) for the session-scoped duration histograms ferrum_stream_duration_ms (TCP/UDP) and ferrum_websocket_session_duration_ms. Same rules as request_duration_buckets_ms.
